fastrcmdcheck

fastrcmdcheck is a much faster drop-in replacement for rcmdcheck and r-lib/actions/check-r-package in CI. It runs the same R CMD check machinery, restructured so that nothing is compiled twice, compiler work is cached between CI runs, and the slow, independent parts of a check run in parallel.

fastrcmdcheck::fastcheck(".", args = "--as-cran", error_on = "warning")
Rscript -e 'fastrcmdcheck::fastcheck_cli()' --as-cran --error-on warning .
# GitHub Actions: replaces r-lib/actions/check-r-package
- uses: grantn5/fastrcmdcheck@main
  with:
    args: "--as-cran"
    error-on: "warning"

Installation

Users

Install with the following

remotes::install_github(
    repo = "grantn5/fastrcmdcheck"
  )

GitHub Actions

Swap r-lib/actions/check-r-package for the action in your existing check workflow. Everything before it (R, dependencies, pandoc) stays the same. The action installs ccache (and sccache for Rust packages), restores the compiler cache, installs fastrcmdcheck and runs the check.

# .github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

name: R-CMD-check

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          use-public-rspm: true
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
        with:
          needs: check
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-pandoc@v2

      # was: - uses: r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2
      - uses: grantn5/fastrcmdcheck@main
        with:
          args: "--as-cran --no-manual"
          error-on: "warning"

Inputs:

Input Default
path "." package directory
args "--as-cran" extra R CMD check arguments, space separated
error-on "warning" never, error, warning or note
profile "faithful" faithful or fast (see Compiler profiles)
jobs all cores number of parallel workers
cache-version "1" bump to throw away the compiler caches
upload-results "true" upload the check directory as an artifact on failure

A common setup is profile: "fast" on pull requests and the default faithful profile on main.

Code format

We use air to keep the code consistent. The style is set in air.toml. To format, run:

air format .

Benchmarks

Wall-clock seconds for --as-cran --no-manual, every run pinned to the same 4 cores (a GitHub runner), measured with bench/bench.sh on 2026-10-26. rcmdcheck -j is rcmdcheck with MAKEFLAGS=-j4. Cold means an empty cache_dir and warm means a second run with an unchanged package. fast is profile = "fast". All scenarios report the same errors, warnings and notes as rcmdcheck.

Package rcmdcheck rcmdcheck -j cold warm fast cold fast warm warm speed-up
cppheavy (C++, many TUs) 93.6 48.4 23.2 15.5 22.8 15.3 6.0x
fs (CRAN 1.6.5, bundled libuv) 51.4 35.4 18.9 13.7 16.9 13.7 3.8x
rheavy (pure R, many tests) 38.5 33.8 12.2 12.3 11.4 11.4 3.1x
rustpkg (Rust via cargo) 30.5 29.0 20.4 15.1 15.1 11.0 2.0x

Most of the warm-run speed-up comes from not compiling again, which doesn’t depend on core count. On fewer cores (e.g. a 2-core runner) the cold builds and the parallel tests (rheavy) slow down, but warm runs keep most of their advantage. The online clock check was off for every tool (see _R_CHECK_SYSTEM_CLOCK_ below). With it on, any tool can lose up to about 60s per run when the time servers can’t be reached.

Why rcmdcheck is slow, and what changes

What rcmdcheck() does, all serially:

  1. R CMD build: installs the package (compile #1) to build the vignettes (vignettes run #1), then builds the PDF manual (LaTeX).
  2. R CMD check: installs the package again from the tarball (compile #2, serial make, no cache), runs ~50 static checks, then the examples, then the whole test suite in one process, then rebuilds the vignettes (vignettes run #2) and the PDF manual again.

C++/Rust code gets compiled twice per run and from scratch on every CI run. Rust crates (with lto = true / codegen-units = 1, as in the common templates) dominate many check runs.

What fastcheck() does:

Step What happens Why it is faster
build R CMD build --no-build-vignettes --no-manual no install, no vignettes, no LaTeX (a few seconds)
install one R CMD INSTALL from a stable staging dir with MAKEFLAGS=-jN, ccache for C/C++, sccache for Rust when available, and the cargo target/ dir saved between runs compiles once, in parallel; on warm runs only changed translation units / crates compile
static checks R CMD check --install=check:<log> --library=<lib> (CRAN’s own “already installed” mode) reuses the install, still analyses the install log for compiler warnings, symbol tables etc.
tests testthat files sharded over N processes (balanced by the previous run’s per-file timings); each shard gets a private copy of tests/; non-testthat tests/*.R run like R CMD check (R CMD BATCH, .Rout.save diffs) the usual bottleneck now runs in parallel
examples Rd examples extracted with tools::Rd2ex() and run in N processes, each in its own working directory, per-topic clean env/RNG/options/devices like R CMD check parallel
vignettes every vignette rebuilt in its own process against the installed package executed once instead of twice, in parallel

Static checks, test shards, example shards and vignettes all run at the same time in one process pool (jobs, default: all cores). The result has errors, warnings and notes like rcmdcheck, plus a checks data frame, timings and the log directory.

Compiler profiles

  • profile = "faithful" (default): R’s compiler flags are untouched, so the install log and the compiler warning checks are the same as R CMD check. All speedups are structural (one compile, parallel make, caching, concurrency).
  • profile = "fast": also compiles C/C++ with -O0 -g0 and Rust with lto=false, codegen-units=256, opt-level=1 (through CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_* env vars, which override Cargo.toml). Much faster cold builds of heavy C++/Rust; meant for PR CI. Optimisation-dependent warnings (e.g. -Wmaybe-uninitialized) can be missed, so keep a faithful job on main and for releases.

Fidelity: what is (and isn’t) identical to R CMD check

  • All static checks are R’s own R CMD check code (--install=check: is the mode CRAN uses for already-installed packages).
  • Test failures, example errors and vignette errors are all reported as ERROR.
  • Differences:
    • Examples: per-topic timings and --timings output are not produced, and Examples/*.Rout.save comparisons are not done.
    • Vignettes are woven (all code runs) but not tangled/re-run separately, and the inst/doc consistency checks of R CMD check are skipped (--ignore-vignettes).
    • testthat shards run in separate processes. Tests that depend on running after another file in the same process (state leaking between files) can behave differently. Tests that write to fixed paths inside tests/ are fine (each shard has its own copy); tests writing to fixed paths elsewhere (e.g. ~) may collide.
    • The PDF manual is skipped unless manual = TRUE / --manual. The Rd checks (checkRd, codoc, usage, cross-references, missing docs) all still run.
    • _R_CHECK_SYSTEM_CLOCK_ defaults to FALSE. With --as-cran, R otherwise asks up to three internet time servers for the current time, one after another, to catch a machine whose clock is wrong. When the servers can’t be reached (common on CI and behind firewalls), each one can take up to 60s before failing, and the check still ends with only “NOTE: unable to verify current time”. With the default, the future file timestamps check still runs, but compares against the system clock (NTP-synced on GitHub runners). Set _R_CHECK_SYSTEM_CLOCK_=TRUE to get R’s behaviour back.

Options

R argument CLI default
args any unknown --flag character()
jobs -j/--jobs, $FASTCHECK_JOBS all cores
profile --profile "faithful"
cache_dir --cache-dir, $FASTCHECK_CACHE_DIR tools::R_user_dir("fastrcmdcheck", "cache")
check_dir --check-dir temp dir
error_on --error-on "never" (R) / "warning" (CLI)
tests, examples, vignettes --no-tests, --no-examples, --no-vignettes TRUE
manual --manual FALSE
timeout --timeout none
--json FILE write results as JSON

CI caching

Persist cache_dir between runs (the action does this with actions/cache). It contains the ccache/sccache stores, the saved cargo target/ dirs, the staged sources and per-file test timings. Install ccache (apt-get install ccache) and, for Rust packages, sccache. The action does both. Package dependencies are still installed by r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies (which already caches).

Rust: the saved target/ dir is reused when the package’s Makevars builds into src/<crate dir>/target (the default layout of rextendr / savvy / the “hellorust” templates). If a Makevars deletes target/ after building (some CRAN-oriented templates do when NOT_CRAN is unset), only sccache helps.

Development 

R CMD INSTALL .
NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local()'
Rscript bench/make-fixtures.R /tmp/fixtures      # synthetic C++ / Rust / R packages
bench/bench.sh /tmp/fixtures /tmp/bench-out 4      # rcmdcheck vs fastcheck on 4 cores
